instruction: Create the directory ~/Test/Speed and save a file named info.txt there with the text 'Network test completed'.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent dismissed privacy popup, ran speed test (clicked GO, waited for completion), navigated to results page, opened terminal, created ~/Test/Speed/results.txt with lowercase metric names (ping, download, upload) instead of capitalized names (Ping, Download, Upload).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal (Ctrl+Alt+T), execute bash commands (mkdir, echo), create directory structures, write content to text files
metadata.failure_analysis: Model used lowercase metric names ('ping', 'download', 'upload') when the evaluator expected capitalized names ('Ping', 'Download', 'Upload') matching the speedtest.net UI display.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed file-creation sub-task: model demonstrated ability to open terminal and create directories/files via bash in the original trajectory. This tests that capability with known expected content, removing the web-scraping variable.
metadata.explanation: Task requires creating directory ~/Test/Speed and writing a file info.txt with exact specified content. Evaluator uses vm_file getter to download the file and file_contains metric to verify the expected text is present.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (vm_file) correctly targets /home/user/Test/Speed/info.txt, which maps to ~/Test/Speed/info.txt as specified in the instruction.
Metric (file_contains) correctly reads the downloaded file and checks that all strings in config['expected'] are present in the file content.
Expected parameter handling is correct: with expected.type='rule', the framework passes the rules dict directly to the metric, so config['expected'] yields ['Network test completed'].

Full coverage: if the file exists at the correct path with the correct content, the directory ~/Test/Speed must also exist. Both instruction requirements (create directory + write file with specific text) are implicitly verified.
The expected text 'Network test completed' exactly matches what the instruction specifies.
